why.stone: The bold display and set numbers are faceted like chiselled inscription letters, while the regular titles stay a calm serif with only a faint hewn edge.
why.carving: The facets on S, 3, 5, 6 and 8 share one polygonal logic and look deliberate, with the 6 bowl cleaner than K3's; 3/8 and 0/O are still easy to tell apart, though a few joins are slightly uneven.
why.calm: Light regular titles and a measured bold give it presence without shouting, and the body text stays quiet.
why.personality: The cut-stone bold numerals are recognisable, though the regular weight reads close to a conventional book serif.

why.stone: Faceted, flat-cut curves on the bold S, 3, 5, 6, 8 and O read clearly as hewn letters on an inscriptional serif skeleton, though the regular titles stay close to a conventional book serif.
why.carving: Facets are applied consistently across bold capitals and digits with crisp straight cuts, 0/O and 3/8 stay distinct, but a few joins (the tip of the 6, the lower bowl of the 5) are slightly lopsided and the regular weight carries the carving only faintly.
why.calm: A measured serif with moderate weight contrast between regular and bold; the cuts add presence without shouting.
why.personality: The polygonal bowls give it a recognisable chiselled voice, though the regular titles fall back toward a generic serif.

why.stone: Faceted bold caps, Squat and set numbers read as hewn inscription, though the regular titles stay a smooth bookish serif.
why.carving: Facets on S, O, 0 and 3/8 are crisp, but the 6 in 62.5 is mostly round with only a few facets so it looks pasted on next to the polygonal 5 and O, and the O/0 are slightly lumpy.
why.calm: Moderate weight and generous serifs keep it steady; the angular bold is present without shouting.
why.personality: The chiselled polygonal bounds give a recognisable voice, slightly diluted by the inconsistent 6.

why.stone: Nearly identical to K1, with faceted bold capitals and digits that read as cut stone.
why.carving: It uses the same polygonal system as K1, but the 6 and 5 bowls show slightly more irregular, lumpy facets, so the cuts look a bit less even and more processed.
why.calm: It has the same quiet regular weight and measured bold, so it is calm with presence.
why.personality: Its faceted numerals have the same distinct voice as K1.

why.stone: Nearly identical to K1: faceted bold capitals and digits read as cut stone over an inscriptional serif base, regular titles less so.
why.carving: Coherent, crisp facets across S, 3, 5, 6, 8 and O with digits easy to tell apart; the 6 and 5 bowls are a touch more evenly polygonal than K1's, but the regular weight still barely shows the cuts.
why.calm: Steady and composed, with the bold giving presence without aggression.
why.personality: Distinct chiselled voice in the bold and numerals, softened by a conventional-looking regular.

why.stone: Same faceted bold display as K1, reading as chiselled stone in Squat, SISIFO and the set numbers, with smooth regular titles.
why.carving: The 6 is faceted like the 5, S, 3, 8 and O, so the bold digits share one coherent cut; facets are crisp though O/0 remain a touch uneven and 0/O stay distinguishable by width.
why.calm: Steady weight and open spacing; angularity adds presence without aggression.
why.personality: Distinct chiselled-polygon voice applied more consistently than K1.
